endorsements.quote: Real-world pilots aligned with MTB guidelines will demonstrate the added value of oncDSTs in improving discussion quality and patient outcomes, with MTB feedback driving ongoing refinement.
Regulatory and reimbursement frameworks must comply with GDPR, IVDR, MDR, and the AI Act, with early deployment data guiding standardised coverage.

It is also important to keep in mind that these implementations will require investment in infrastructure, specialised personnel, cybersecurity, database maintenance, and quality assurance, but are expected to be cost-effective under the assumption that standardised, data-driven decision support will optimise care, reduce ineffective treatments, improve clinical productivity, and lower long-term healthcare costs.
To support this, CAN.HEAL recommends a phased deployment strategy ( Figure 3 ), ensuring that each step contributes to a cohesive, patient-centred, and future-proof learning system.

unlisted_practices: Harmonise variant annotation and classification across oncology decision support tools.
Ensure AI interpretability and transparency in oncology decision support tools.
Achieve interoperability of oncology decision support tools with hospital EHR/LIMS systems using a common data model.
Implement automated clinical trial matching based on genomic and clinical data.
Use a regulatory sandbox to test and validate innovative AI solutions under regulatory supervision.
Engage payers and patient groups early to guide implementation of decision support tools.
Implement follow-up modules to monitor performance and update recommendations of AI decision support tools.
Harmonise MTB report formats regardless of the decision support tool used.
Adapt oncology decision support tools to local clinical guidelines, national drug repositories, and reimbursement schemes.

screen.reason: This paper presents the conceptual EU-oncDST digital framework and recommendations/action plan for implementing interoperable oncology decision support tools and AI in Europe, rather than testing a specific empirical deployment.
